title: The popular story. A newspaper called Alfred Nobel the merchant of death.
description:
A newspaper called Alfred Nobel the merchant of death. In 1888 his brother Ludvig died in France, and a French paper is said to have mistaken it for Alfred's death.

Alfred's brother, who died in France that year. The death is the part of the story that is not in doubt.

Nobody has found the obituary. Historians have not located an original copy, and some now treat the story as a myth.

Signed his final will on 27 November at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, leaving his estate to fund five prizes.

The motives are still debated. The Nobel Foundation points to an 1868 award from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences as a possible origin of the science prizes. The peace prize is often linked to his friendship with Bertha von Suttner.

The best known origin story is the one nobody can show you.

Sources:
- https://www.history.com/news/did-a-premature-obituary-inspire-the-nobel-prize (read): established the usual story (Ludvig Nobel died in France in 1888 and a French paper mistook it for Alfred's death, calling him a merchant of death), that historians have not found an original copy of that obituary, that some now treat it as a myth, that the Nobel Foundation suggests an 1868 award from the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences as a possible origin of the science prizes, and that Nobel met Bertha von Suttner in 1876 and signed his will on 27 November 1895.
- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Nobel (read): corroborated that Ludvig died in 1888, that the obituary story is described as supposedly causing newspapers to publish obituaries of Alfred in error and that historians have been unable to verify it, and that the will was signed on 27 November 1895 at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris.
- https://www.nobelprize.org/alfred-nobel/alfred-nobels-will/ (read): primary institutional source. Established that the third and final will was signed on 27 November 1895 at the Swedish-Norwegian Club in Paris, that it funds five prizes (physics, chemistry, physiology or medicine, literature and peace), and that the first prizes were awarded in 1901.
